properties.accuracy_caveat: The outline is Assessor lot 9900054, so its edges are recorded lot lines, not a trace. DataSF lists the pier as its own lot, 9900054 (block 9900, with the pier number as the lot), and the earlier hand trace lies 92% inside it, so the match is clear; no Port document read names the lot. The lot's edge can run a few metres off the visible deck edge, and the lot is the legal boundary, not the deck and shed. Status and use are as shown on this record.
properties.why_no_real_parcel: Pier 54 has its own Assessor lot, 9900054 (DataSF Parcels, acdm-wktn, active), and this record's outline is that lot.
properties.regulatory_context: Red-tagged in early July 2024 (SFGate, Sept 2024); Port Engineering recommended closing the pier to the public and tenants for safety reasons, and its 11 tenants were told to vacate by the end of 2024 (Port memo, Aug 9, 2024, written before that date). The Port's draft Five-Year Capital Improvement Program (FY2027-31, Feb 2026) proposes a 'Pier 54 Shed Demolition' line item totaling $2.0M ($500,000 in FY2026-27 and $1,500,000 in FY2027-28); it is a proposed budget line, no source read says demolition has started, and no line item for full substructure removal appears in that document.
properties.notes: Pier 54's outline is Assessor lot 9900054 (see the accuracy note). This is a Port maritime/pier facility, not an OCII Mission Bay South development block -- grouped under the Mission Bay South site here because that is the nearest tracked site and because DataSF's official 'Former San Francisco Redevelopment Agency Project Areas' boundary for Mission Bay South extends north along the Terry A. Francois Blvd shoreline to include this stretch. It is materially farther from Mission Rock's own tracked footprint (Pier 48/50, ~470m away) than from Mission Bay South's nearest tracked features (the UCSF Illinois Street Garage/P24 lawn, ~30m away). Recorded as adjacent rather than tracked because it is Port-jurisdiction maritime infrastructure, not a Mission Bay OCII development parcel like this site's other tracked records. A derelict timber pier stands just north of this footprint, separate from it (probably Pier 52, a separate Port asset; the identification is not confirmed by a source and it is not part of this record).
